statements: Each obligation in the instruction is its own type under “Pedestrian Bridge Structural Review”.
“Site and Geotechnical Survey” produces the site survey and the geotechnical report.
“Structural Form Options Study” compares the viable structural forms against the site survey and the geotechnical report, and selects one.

“Load Analysis (pedestrian, wind, vibration)” analyses the selected form to the Eurocodes for pedestrian, wind and pedestrian-induced vibration loading, and consumes the geotechnical report because foundation stiffness affects the dynamic model.
“Member, Connection and Foundation Design” designs the members, connections and foundations from the load model and the geotechnical report.

“Independent Design Check” is declared DELEGATED_EXTERNAL, so a firm that took no part in the design carries it out, as the rail authority requires; it certifies the design calculations and drawings, and also consumes the geotechnical report.

“Rail Authority Permit Submission” consumes the check certificate, so the submission cannot be made before the independent check exists; it also consumes the geotechnical report and the design calculations.
The Eurocodes (EN 1991-2 and EN 1993-2) with the national annex apply.
A firm with no role in the design satisfies the rail authority’s independence requirement.
Fabrication, erection and site supervision are outside the instruction and are not modelled.

The soft clay layer 3 m below the north abutment may require piled foundations; the geotechnical report will decide, which is why the options study, the load analysis, the design and the independent check all consume it.
